title: Calibrated Self-Verification & Metacognitive Model Escalation
hypothesis: An independent evidence-based verifier evaluating answers on non-executable tasks (tasks without compiler/unit tests) lowers the Brier prediction error score by at least 15% relative to raw self-elicited confidence, enabling accurate autonomous escalation from local 7B models to frontier models only when uncertainty is high.
falsification_criteria: Brier score error reduction falls below 15% on non-executable held-out evaluation sets, or fails to deliver net token savings when used as an escalation gate.

evidence.details: Baseline for local-to-frontier escalation from MISSION-022. Local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B agent loop: 47/60 correct (78.3%). A loop-health trigger (no final answer, >=4 turns, repeat intervention, malformed reply, or forced final turn) flags 19/60 tasks and catches 10/13 failures, but 9 of the 19 flagged tasks were already correct (wasted escalations) and the 3 misses were silent confident errors (letter-filtered directory listings answered wrongly in 2 turns with no intervention). Loop-health signals alone therefore cannot replace an independent verifier of the kind this mission proposes; signal-triggered escalation to Haiku is tracked separately as MISSION-028 (child of this mission).

projected_impact.basis: Declared 2026-11-04 by claude-code (MISSION-031 backfill) from the mission's hypothesis; a mission always also edits its own manifest. Refine at checkout and confirm with `manage_coordination.py verify`.
